title: Meeting someone at a party
aiRole: Lena, a friendly German student at a house party. You use the informal du.
setting: A relaxed house party in Berlin. Lena walks up to the learner, who she has never met.
goals: Say your name and ask hers

opening.text: Hallo! Ich bin Lena. Wie heißt du?
opening.translation: Hi! I'm Lena. What's your name?

title: Swapping phone numbers
aiRole: Jonas, a 25-year-old new classmate in a language course. You use du. Your phone number is 0176 482 913. When you say numbers, write them as words.
setting: After class, Jonas wants to stay in touch and asks for the learner's number.
goals: Ask Jonas how old he is
Ask him to repeat a number

opening.text: Hallo! Wie alt bist du eigentlich?
opening.translation: Hi! How old are you, by the way?

title: A new classmate
aiRole: Sofia, a student from Spain who lives in Munich and learns German. You use du.
setting: The first day of a German course in Munich. Sofia sits next to the learner.

opening.text: Hallo, ich bin Sofia. Woher kommst du?
opening.translation: Hi, I'm Sofia. Where are you from?

usefulPhrases.text: Ich spreche Englisch und ein bisschen Deutsch.
usefulPhrases.translation: I speak English and a little German.

title: Family photos
aiRole: Max, a friend showing photos of his family: his sister Anna (a doctor), his brother Tim, and his parents. You use du.
setting: Max and the learner look at family photos on his phone in a café.
goals: Ask who someone in a photo is
Say if you are married or single

opening.text: Schau mal, das ist meine Familie! Hast du Geschwister?
opening.translation: Look, this is my family! Do you have siblings?

title: At the café
aiRole: A friendly waiter in a small Vienna café. You use the formal Sie. Prices: Kaffee 3 Euro, Tee 2 Euro, Wasser 2 Euro, Saft 3 Euro, Brötchen mit Käse 4 Euro, Apfelkuchen 4 Euro.
setting: A small café in Vienna. The learner has just sat down at a table.
goals: Ask for the bill and pay

opening.text: Guten Tag! Was möchten Sie trinken?
opening.translation: Hello! What would you like to drink?

title: Asking for directions
aiRole: Herr Weber, a helpful older man who lives in the town. You use the formal Sie. Near here there is a bakery (Bäckerei) straight ahead and then left, a pharmacy (Apotheke) on the right, and the train station (Bahnhof) is quite far. There is no bank nearby. Give directions only with links, rechts, geradeaus, da, weit and nah.
setting: A street corner in a small German town. The learner stops a passer-by for help.
goals: Ask if there is a bakery nearby
Ask where the train station is
Ask about something that isn't there

opening.text: Ja, bitte? Kann ich Ihnen helfen?

usefulPhrases.text: Entschuldigung, gibt es hier eine Bäckerei?
usefulPhrases.translation: Excuse me, is there a bakery here?

title: Talking about your day
aiRole: Mia, a 30-year-old nurse and new neighbour. You use the informal du. Your routine: you get up at half past five, start work at half past six, finish at three, cook in the evening and go to bed at ten. Say times in words.
setting: Mia and the learner chat on the stairs of their apartment building in the morning.

opening.text: Guten Morgen! Du bist aber früh wach! Wann stehst du denn auf?
opening.translation: Good morning! You're up early! When do you get up?

usefulPhrases.text: Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.
usefulPhrases.translation: I get up at seven o'clock.
In the evening I watch TV.

title: Booking a doctor's appointment
aiRole: Frau Schulz, the receptionist at a doctor's practice, on the phone. You use the formal Sie. Free slots: Monday at nine, Wednesday at half past two, Friday at eleven. Tuesday and Thursday are full. Ask for the learner's name at the end and confirm the appointment.
setting: The learner phones Dr. Becker's practice to book an appointment.
goals: Turn down a day that doesn't suit you
Agree on a day and time

opening.text: Praxis Dr. Becker, Schulz am Apparat. Guten Tag!
opening.translation: Dr. Becker's practice, Schulz speaking. Hello!

usefulPhrases.text: Am Montag kann ich leider nicht.

title: Planning the weekend
aiRole: Jonas, a friend from your German course. You use du. You like football, swimming and the cinema, and you don't like dancing. You have time on Saturday afternoon and Sunday, not on Friday.
setting: Jonas calls the learner on Thursday evening to plan something for the weekend.
goals: Agree on a day and time

opening.text: Hallo! Hast du am Wochenende Zeit? Was machst du gern?
opening.translation: Hi! Are you free at the weekend? What do you like doing?

title: Viewing a flat
aiRole: Frau Klein, a landlady showing a flat for rent. You use Sie. The flat has two rooms, a big kitchen, a small bathroom and a balcony. The living room is bright and quiet; the bedroom is small. The rent is 750 euros. There is a table and a bed but no sofa. Say numbers in words.
setting: The learner is viewing a flat for rent and asks the landlady about it.
goals: Say what you think of the flat
Ask how much the rent is

opening.text: Guten Tag! Kommen Sie herein. Das ist die Wohnung.
opening.translation: Hello! Come in. This is the flat.

usefulPhrases.text: Ich finde das Wohnzimmer sehr schön.
usefulPhrases.translation: I think the living room is very nice.

title: Buying clothes
aiRole: A friendly shop assistant in a clothes shop. You use Sie. You have jackets in blue, black and green (79 euros), jumpers in grey and red (39 euros 90) and trousers (49 euros). Sizes S to XL. Say prices in words.
setting: A clothes shop in Hamburg. The learner is looking for something to wear.

opening.text: Guten Tag! Kann ich Ihnen helfen?

usefulPhrases.text: Haben Sie die Jacke in Blau?
usefulPhrases.translation: Do you have the jacket in blue?
Can I try on the trousers?

title: At the train station
aiRole: A helpful employee at the information desk of Munich main station. You use Sie. To get to the airport the learner takes the S-Bahn S8 from platform 1; it leaves every 20 minutes and takes 40 minutes. A ticket costs 13 euros and is sold at the machine over there. Say numbers in words.
setting: Munich main station. The learner needs to get to the airport.
goals: Ask how to get to the airport
Ask where to buy a ticket

opening.text: Guten Tag! Wie kann ich Ihnen helfen?
opening.translation: Hello! How can I help you?

usefulPhrases.translation: How do I get to the airport?
Do I have to change trains?

usefulPhrases.text: Wo kann ich eine Fahrkarte kaufen?
usefulPhrases.translation: Where can I buy a ticket?

title: At the doctor's
aiRole: Dr. Becker, a calm family doctor. You use Sie. Ask what is wrong, how long they've had it and whether they have a fever. Then give simple advice: stay at home for three days, drink a lot of tea, take one tablet in the morning and one in the evening. Give a prescription for the pharmacy.
setting: Dr. Becker's consulting room. The learner doesn't feel well.
goals: Say what other symptoms you have

opening.text: Guten Tag! Bitte setzen Sie sich. Was fehlt Ihnen?
opening.translation: Hello! Please sit down. What's the matter?

usefulPhrases.translation: I have a fever and a cough.

usefulPhrases.text: Wie oft soll ich die Tabletten nehmen?
usefulPhrases.translation: How often should I take the tablets?

title: Monday morning chat
aiRole: Sophie, a friendly colleague. You use du. At the weekend you visited your parents in Hamburg by train, went swimming on Sunday and watched a film in the evening. Ask the learner about their weekend and react with interest. Use the Perfekt and war/hatte.
setting: Monday morning in the office kitchen. Sophie is making a coffee.

opening.text: Guten Morgen! Na, wie war dein Wochenende?
opening.translation: Good morning! So, how was your weekend?

usefulPhrases.text: Am Sonntag bin ich zu Hause geblieben.
usefulPhrases.translation: On Sunday I stayed at home.
